definitions.explanation: A surface that is flat and level, without curves or elevations. Used both in everyday language for flat surfaces and in mathematics and geometry for a two-dimensional plane.

examples.japanese: {平面|へいめん}に{線|せん}を{引|ひ}く。
examples.english: To draw a line on a flat surface.

examples.japanese: {平面|へいめん}{図|ず}で{間取|まど}りを{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.english: To check the floor layout on a plan view.

examples.japanese: {数学|すうがく}では、{二|ふた}つの{平面|へいめん}が{交|まじ}わると{直線|ちょくせん}ができる。
examples.english: In mathematics, when two planes intersect, a straight line is formed.

notes:
A flat, two-dimensional surface. Composed of {平|へい} (flat/level) + {面|めん} (surface/face). Used in everyday language, architecture, and mathematics.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平面|へいめん}{図|ず}: floor plan; plan view
- {平面|へいめん}{幾何学|きかがく}: plane geometry
- {平面|へいめん}{的|てき}: flat; two-dimensional (also figuratively: lacking depth)
- {平面|へいめん}{交差|こうさ}: at-grade intersection (roads crossing on the same level)
- {平面|へいめん}{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}: surface-level parking lot

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {立体|りったい}: three-dimensional object — the conceptual opposite of {平面|へいめん}
- {表面|ひょうめん}: surface — refers to the outer face of an object, not necessarily flat
- {水平|すいへい}: horizontal; level — describes orientation rather than dimensionality

USAGE:
When used as a modifier ({平面|へいめん}{的|てき}), it can describe something figuratively as lacking depth or dimensionality, such as a flat, uninteresting character in a novel.
